title: Changing the Subject of a Formula
seo_title: Year 8 Rearranging Formulae Worksheets: Changing the Subject, Two-Step, Squares and Roots
standard_text: Understand and use standard mathematical formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject; substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions, including scientific formulae.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 worksheets on changing the subject of a formula: one-step and two-step rearranging, brackets and fractions, real formulae with squares and roots, and using rearranged formulae. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rearrange like solving an equation: use inverse operations and undo the last operation first.
key_sub: y = 4x + 7 becomes x = (y − 7)/4: subtract 7 first, then divide everything by 4.
body_html:
How it works

The subject of a formula is the letter on its own, such as A in A = lw. To change the subject, treat the formula like an equation: use inverse operations on both sides, undoing the last operation first.

Example

Make x the subject of y = 4x + 7.

Subtract 7: y − 7 = 4x.

Divide by 4.

Answer: x = (y − 7)/4

Example

Make h the subject of A = ½bh.

Multiply by 2: 2A = bh.

Divide by b.

Answer: h = 2A/b

Example

Make r the subject of A = πr2.

Divide by π.

Square root.

Answer: r = √(A/π)

Common mistakes

  • Doing the same operation instead of the inverse: y = x + 3 gives x = y − 3, not y + 3.
  • Undoing in the wrong order: for y = 2x + 6, subtract 6 before dividing by 2.
  • Dividing only one term: (y − 6)/2 is not the same as y/2 − 6.
  • Square rooting only part of an expression: x = √(y − 5), not √y − 5.

faq.q: What does changing the subject of a formula mean?
faq.a: Rearranging it so a different letter is on its own. A = lw can be rearranged to w = A/l.

faq.q: How is rearranging like solving an equation?
faq.a: You use the same inverse operations on both sides, but you finish with letters instead of a number.

faq.q: Which operation do I undo first?
faq.a: The last one that was done to the letter. In y = 4x + 7, x is multiplied by 4 and then 7 is added, so subtract 7 first.

faq.q: How do I undo a square?
faq.a: Take the square root of the whole other side. From y = x² + 5, x = √(y − 5).

items.e: The subject is the letter on its own on one side: A.

items.q: To make x the subject of y = 4x + 7, what should you do first?
items.e: Undo the operations in reverse order: the + 7 was last, so subtract 7 first.

items.q: Oliver makes x the subject of y = 2x + 6 and gets x = y/2 − 6. What is the correct answer?
items.e: Subtract 6 first, then divide everything by 2: x = (y − 6) ÷ 2. Oliver only divided y.
